expotigla.title: ExpoTigla
expotigla.subtitle: Online shop for complete roofing systems
about: ExpoTigla sells roofing materials for homes and industrial buildings, plus consultancy, material calculations and installation. The site had to show that the company doesn't just sell metal sheets, it sells the whole system, and get visitors to a quote or an order as quickly as possible.
We built a restrained visual identity in gold and anthracite grey, with large photos of roofs and a structure that's easy to follow: from categories to products, then on to the quote request.
sections: The first screen says straight away what the company does: complete roofing systems. A large image, a short message and a single main button. Below the hero, a strip with four selling points: technical advice, material calculations, guaranteed delivery and products with a warranty.

The range is split into visual categories (metal roof tiles, standing seam sheets, sandwich panels, rainwater systems, flashings, ventilation, membranes, screws and more). Each card has a photo, a title and a one-line description, so visitors can quickly find the right category.
A carousel of popular products: a variant label, category, price shown as a range (‘from…’) and two clear actions: ‘Details’ and ‘Add to cart’.
A section dedicated to services: free consultation, material calculations, installation on request and finishing recommendations. Two buttons lead to the services page and to the configurator.
An illustration of the roof ‘taken apart’ into its components explains the idea of a complete system and links to the configurator.

A separate page for the configurator, with a layer-by-layer diagram of the roof and the message ‘1 project, 1 quote, 1 consultant’. Below the hero come the partner brands and the benefits of an all-in-one quote.
A grid of 8 numbered components (roof covering, flashings, rainwater system, membranes, ventilation, fixings, delivery, installation), each with the option to include it in the quote.
Four cards with the company's guarantees (certified quality, delivery in 24–72h, warranty of up to 30 years, technical support), followed by a carousel of Google reviews.

A gold strip with a clear call to action: send your roof dimensions and get a free quote within 24 hours. The footer groups the products, company pages, contact details, areas served and the ANPC/SOL links.
features: Product catalogue with variants and prices including VAT

cosmin-tatulescu.title: Cosmin Tătulescu
cosmin-tatulescu.subtitle: Business website with bookings for Christmas photo sessions
about: Christmas sessions are a seasonal service, with a short booking window and lots of repeat questions from parents. The site had to answer them before they were asked: what you get, how much it costs, when there's availability and where the studio is.

We went for an airy design, with a white and cream background, elegant serif headings and subtle touches of Christmas red. Everything sits on one long page with a fixed menu, so visitors can jump straight to prices, the calendar or the gallery. The site also has an English version.
sections: A real photo of the studio set, alongside the heading ‘Christmas photo sessions 2026 in Brașov’ and a warm text about the atmosphere of the session. The main button goes straight to the available days.
A short section that sets the tone: no smiles on command, just the family as it really is.

Four columns with big, easy-to-read numbers: 45 minutes, 35–50 photos, 3 sets and delivery in about a week, in a private online gallery. Underneath, the offer of prints and canvases, presented as a gift for relatives.
The price goes up the closer you get to Christmas, which encourages early bookings. Each period has a short label, some of them with a touch of humour.
A calendar split into the price periods, with the number of free slots for each day. Two clear options: book a session or give a session as a gift.
A selection of photos from previous sessions, with a link to the full gallery.
The address, a landmark, opening hours and nearby towns and villages. The Google map only loads on request, and visitors are told that this means Google receives their IP address.
Nine questions parents often ask (clothing, payment, cancellation, photo delivery, gift sessions), grouped in a compact accordion.
A simple form with consent to data processing, plus phone, email and social media. The page ends with a holiday message and one more button to the available days.
features: Booking calendar with free slots per day
Different prices depending on the period
Google map loaded only with the visitor's consent

traditum.title: Traditum By Victoria
traditum.subtitle: Business website for an artisan patisserie, with quote requests
about: Traditum By Victoria mainly works to order: personalised cakes, dessert tables for weddings and christenings, gift boxes. Most products don't have a fixed price, so the site isn't an online shop. Its job is to build trust and lead visitors to a quote request.

We went for a warm palette of cream and dark brown, with gold accents, and serif headings that match the idea of a ‘taste of yesteryear’. Product photos take up most of the page, and the ‘Request a quote’ button is always visible in the menu.
sections: The main message, ‘Artisan desserts with the taste of yesteryear’, with a short description of what's on offer and two actions: see the products or request a quote.

Five categories (cakes, candy bar, gift boxes, tags, mărțișor charms), each with a photo, a short description and either a price or the label ‘Price on request’, for products priced according to the event.

A short section about the bakehouse and the patisserie's philosophy, with four benefits (quality, personalised cakes, online orders, home delivery). Below it, a strip of numbers: 10+ years of experience, 80+ recipes, 120+ varieties, 2500+ customers.
Four short customer reviews, with a link to the page with all the reviews.
Final call to action and footer
A dark block that invites visitors to ask for a personalised quote for their event. The footer has the address, phone number, email, main links and legal pages.
A grid of photos of dessert tables and desserts made for customers' events. It shows visitors real results, not stock photos.
A quote request form with fields for the type of event and details (date, number of servings, theme), alongside the contact details, opening hours by day and a button straight to WhatsApp.
features: Catalogue by category, with prices or ‘price on request’
Quote request form tailored to events
Frequently asked questions on the contact page

mrdtf.title: Mr.DTF
mrdtf.subtitle: Business website with an order form for DTF printing by the linear metre
meta: Business website with an order form
about: Mr.DTF's customers are mostly companies and creators who customise textiles. They want to find out three things fast: how much it costs, how much fits on the film and how to send the file. The site answers all three on a single page, with no unnecessary steps.

The identity starts from the colourful, graffiti-style logo. The rest of the design is clean and bright, with yellow accents on the order buttons and large, easy-to-read headings. For a playful touch, we added an interactive T-shirt to the hero: visitors drag a print onto the T-shirt and instantly see how it would look.
sections: The main message, ‘Quality DTF prints’, puts the 90 cm width front and centre. Right below are the five price tiers per linear metre, with the price dropping as the order grows. The best-value tier is highlighted.
Visitors pick one of five prints and drag it onto the T-shirt. A small touch that makes the page memorable and shows exactly what the product does.

You choose the format (A5, A4, A3 or 5–20 cm squares) and see how many pieces fit on one metre of film, plus the estimated price per piece at the first and last price tiers. A visual diagram shows how the designs are laid out on the film.
What we do and how it works
A grid of workshop photos (film, rolls, colours, the Epson printer) and a four-step process: you send your order, we print it, you receive the parcel, you apply it.

Two cards: one leads to the blog (application tips, file preparation, washing), the other to the collection address, with a map. The footer has the contact details, opening hours, company details and legal pages.

A window with everything needed for an order: contact details, linear metres, individual or company, billing details, a link to the artwork and notes. A message explains what happens after you submit: file confirmation, the invoice and printing once payment is received.
features: Quantity-based price tiers, shown on the first screen
Calculator for how much fits on 1 linear metre, by format
Order form with billing details for individuals and companies

comstore.title: ComStore Acoperișuri
comstore.subtitle: Business website for a roof installation and renovation company
about: ComStore handles everything from measuring up to final installation, including the cost estimate and a 3D rendering of the roof. The typical customer is building a house or renovating their roof and wants to know whether they can trust the team. The site answers that with clearly explained services, real projects, testimonials and well-known brands.
We used the logo's colours, yellow and anthracite grey, with large photos of roofs. The ‘Get a quote’ button is always visible in the menu, and phone and WhatsApp are just a click away.
sections: A full-width slider with the message ‘Everything you need for your roof’ and two actions: get a quote or see the products. Below it, a yellow strip with buttons to call and to request a quote.
Five services presented in cards with a photo and a short description: installation, renovation, measurements, cost estimates and 3D renderings.
A section on a dark background with six numbered points: expertise, quality renovations, precise measurements, clear estimates, meeting deadlines and a warranty.
Real jobs, each with the name of the material used (for example Lindab double standing seam sheet), so visitors can see what the product looks like once installed.
Six short reviews, with first name, surname initial and town.
Call to action, partners and footer
A yellow strip with the final call to action for a quote, then the partner logos (Lindab, Velux, Metigla, Wetterbest). The footer has the company details, contact information and the full menu.
features: Hero slider with campaigns (for example, a voucher)
Separate pages for products, projects, campaigns and the blog

apg-garage.title: APG Garage
apg-garage.subtitle: Business website with customer accounts and online bookings for a car repair garage
about: At a car repair garage, people want to find out three things fast: what repairs are done, roughly how much they cost and when they can come in. The site answers all three. It has a list of guide prices by category and an online booking system, so customers no longer have to queue.

We chose a dark, almost black design, with dramatic workshop photos and condensed, all-caps headings. The feel is that of a professional garage. The ‘Book now’ button appears twice on the home page, and WhatsApp is always available.
sections: A full-screen photo of a mechanic at work, the garage's name in large letters and two actions: online booking and prices.

Four main services in simple cards (full service, computer diagnostics, braking system, suspension and steering), with a link to the full list. Below them, three numbers: 10+ years of experience, 500+ customers, 100% transparency.
A section for customer feedback, with stars and a quote.
Call to action and opening hours
A second workshop photo, with the call to action ‘Your car, in good hands’, followed by clearly displayed opening hours.
The services, areas served and car makes repaired, also written with local searches in mind (car repair garage Militari, Sector 6), plus the company details and legal pages.
Guide prices grouped by category, such as services or brakes, noting whether parts are paid for separately. A note explains that the final price is set after diagnostics.
features: List of guide prices by category
Footer text optimised for local searches

asociatia-roa.title: Asociația RO Administrația
asociatia-roa.subtitle: Business website for an NGO working in education and employment
about: The association works with very different audiences: unemployed young people, adults retraining for a new career, employers and public institutions. Each of them is looking for something different on the site. The structure gives everyone a quick route from the very first screen: European projects, counselling or jobs.
We chose an institutional blue palette, a nod to the European Union and EU funding, with airy serif headings. The tone is serious but approachable.
sections: The association's mission, shown in large type, followed by three cards that sort visitors by what they're looking for: European projects, career counselling and jobs.
What you should know about us
Three columns with images that sum up the association's work: EU-funded programmes, personalised counselling and an open community.
Who we work with and what we offer
Two clear lists: who can benefit (young people, job seekers, employers) and what they actually get. Below them, a strip with a call to action to get in touch.
Six cards on a blue background, each with an icon, a description and its own button: vocational training, career guidance, job placement, European projects, partnerships and volunteer recruitment.
Animated counters with the association's results (people counselled, young people qualified, rural communities, partners), followed by the contact details and the NGO's registration details.
features: Quick access for three types of visitor
Dedicated sections for jobs, projects, news and FAQ

wsd-tractari.title: WSD Logistics
wsd-tractari.subtitle: Landing page for a 24/7 car towing company
about: Anyone landing on a towing website is usually at the side of the road, on their phone and stressed. They don't have time to read; they just want a phone number and the reassurance that someone is coming. The site puts the number in the menu, in the yellow bar, in a fixed on-screen button and in the final section. Next to it are quick buttons for WhatsApp and for sending your location.

The design uses black and yellow, the warning colours of road traffic, with large, condensed headings that are easy to read even on the move. The hero photo shows a real vehicle from the company's fleet.
sections: The message ‘Car towing anywhere, any time’, with the ‘Call now’ button front and centre and three key figures: 24/7 service, average arrival time and the number of cities covered. On the right, a photo of the company's flatbed truck in action.
A yellow strip with the phone number in large type and a link for sending your location.
Six services presented in a grid: cars, vans and machinery, SUVs and 4x4s, motorway assistance, roadside assistance and flatbed transport.
Four selling points (fast response, transparent prices, nationwide coverage, ARR-authorised company) and the list of cities served, shown as yellow tags and also designed with local searches in mind.
Reviews and final call to action
Three short reviews, with the city, followed by a yellow block, ‘Stuck on the road?’, with a single call button.
The services, pages for the main cities and the contact details.
features: Fixed call button, always visible on screen
Quick buttons for WhatsApp and sending your location
Dedicated city links for local SEO
